story.name: ジョニーの たび
story.title: Washed Up Again
story.line: ジョニーが タイペイの よいちの はなしを します
story.ja: 朝の浜辺で、ちゃちゃまるがずぶぬれのジョニーを見つける。夜、たき火を囲んで、ジョニーは台北の夜市の話をする。行列のできる胡椒餅、臭豆腐、タピオカミルクティーのおばあさん。でも、その夜市で大事な真鍮のコンパスをなくしてしまった。

segments.en: It was a quiet morning on the island, the kind where the tide is low and the sand is still cool from the night.
Dom was out for his morning run when he spotted something blue and white near the water.
At first he thought it was a pile of old laundry. Then the pile of laundry started to snore.
Whoa, whoa. Hey, buddy, are you okay? You're kind of soaked, man.
The laundry sat up, blinked at the sky, and fixed a sailor's cap that had seen much better days.
Ah, good morning, sailor! Tell me, is this Hawaii? It feels a little bit like Hawaii.
Nope, it's just our island. But hey, welcome back, Gulliver. This is, like, your fifth time.
Gulliver did not remember the island. He never did, no matter how many times he washed up on it. But he remembered the coffee.
By evening, word had gotten around. A small fire was crackling on the beach, and a few neighbors had come down with mugs of cocoa.
So, where were you this time? Last time it was Peru? Portugal? Someplace with a P.
Taiwan! Taipei, to be exact. And let me tell you, I have never eaten so well in my whole life.
His ship had docked near Taipei for two nights. On the first evening, the captain told the crew to go find their own dinner.
So Gulliver followed the crowd, and the crowd led him to a night market on a long, narrow street near the river.
At one end there's this temple, all lit up in red and gold. And from there, the food stalls just go on and on.
The air was warm and smelled like a hundred dinners at once. Grilled squid. Sweet sausage. Something fried.
The first thing he noticed was a line. A long one. Maybe thirty people, all waiting patiently in front of one tiny stall.
Now, I have a rule. If the locals get in line for something, you get in line too. No questions asked.
At the front, a man was pressing balls of dough onto the inside wall of a big clay oven.
They were pepper buns. Crispy and golden on the outside, and inside, juicy pork with lots of green onion and black pepper.
I took one big bite, and it was so hot I burned my tongue. Totally worth it, though. Every single time.
Hold on. Every single time? How many did you have, exactly?
Four. Possibly five. A sailor doesn't count, my dear. A sailor simply enjoys.
A little farther down, he walked past a stall where the smell hit him like a wave. Strong, sharp, and honestly, a bit like old socks.
Stinky tofu. They call it that right on the sign. At least they're honest about it.
Dude, no way. Did you actually try it? I'd be way too scared, honestly.
Of course I did. Smells like a gym bag, tastes like heaven. Crispy outside, soft inside, with pickled cabbage on top.
Later, with tired feet, he stopped at a little drink stand run by an older woman with very quick hands.
She made him a milk tea with chewy tapioca pearls at the bottom, and asked him, in careful English, where he was from.
I said, I'm from the sea, ma'am. She laughed and said everybody's from somewhere. Then she gave me extra pearls.
He sat on a low plastic stool and watched the crowd go by, couples and families and students, all of them in no hurry at all.
Somewhere in all that happiness, he took his old brass compass out of his pocket to check the way back to the ship.
And that, he said, was the very last time he ever saw it.
Oh no, your compass? Is that how you ended up here again?
Well, one thing led to another, as they say. But that, my friends, is a story for tomorrow night.
And with that, Gulliver pulled his cap down over his eyes and fell asleep before the fire burned down.
Dom put a blanket over him. And the waves kept coming in, slow and steady, all night long.

predict.ask: あしたの よる、ジョニーは どんな はなしを する？
choices: He tells them how he got snowed in at a cabin in Vermont.
He finds his compass in his pocket after all.
He opens a pepper bun stall on the beach.
